newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases on corporate dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases on corporate dollar demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling eased marginally against the dollar on Wednesday as demand from corporate importers picked up, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.27 from 55.26 against the dollar. On the pound, the shilling was posted at 91.45 from 91.43.
Dealers said there was some significant demand from the oil companies trading at 55.27/32 levels.
"The oil companies were buying today (Wednesday) morning, hoping to cover commitments for early next year," a dealer said.
Some dealers said that despite the rise in demand, the market remained largely unchanged because dollars from tea and coffee exporters were still flowing in.
"Many interbank dealers were still in long dollar positions, which they had acquired from importers," one dealer said.
A dealer said trade was expected to remain at a low ebb in coming days, with many firms gearing up for the holidays.
"The market is pretty thin, trading in very low volumes. In fact, inflows have eased slightly," another dealer added.
The money market was a bit tight with a good number of banks lending. Overnight rates were quoted at 18 percent from Tuesday's 18-20 percent.
